description: ZALF published long-term soil hydrological observations from its Müncheberg experimental station in the Pleistocene end-moraine landscape of northeast Germany. The experiment compares plough and no-till systems. Suction-cup samples measure soil-water nitrate, and the observations support estimates of deep drainage and nitrate loss. The named ZALF GeoNode page opened publicly, while DataCite lists CSV files and CC BY 4.0 without an indicated fee. Water and food-supply modellers could use the observations to check soil-water, leaching or irrigation simulations under different tillage practices. The metadata does not state exact start and end dates or the frequency of every measurement, so temporal coverage remains uncertain. One experimental station cannot establish behaviour for all German soils. No CSV was downloaded, and the visible map menu did not show a direct file link. This is related to the six-year Müncheberg crop trial G4-0568, but has a distinct DOI and a soil-drainage focus. The prior water-sector candidate rejection did not account for its model-verification role.
